sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The Paris Olympics kicked off last week, and the opening ceremonies were something else.
sentences.zh: 巴黎奥运会上周拉开帷幕，开幕式真是别具一格。

sentences.en: They were awesome.
sentences.zh: 简直太棒了。

sentences.en: The metal band Gojira blasted pyrotechnics from a castle alongside a headless Marie Antoinette.
sentences.zh: 重金属乐队“哥吉拉”在一座城堡旁伴随着无头玛丽·安托瓦内特的形象燃放了烟火。

sentences.en: Celine Dion sang at the base of the Eiffel Tower.
sentences.zh: 席琳·迪翁在埃菲尔铁塔脚下献唱。

sentences.en: A masked torchbearer ran on the rooftops like Tom Cruise in Mission Impossible.
sentences.zh: 一个戴面具的火炬手像《碟中谍》里的汤姆·克鲁斯一样在屋顶上奔跑。

sentences.en: And yes, there was an animal cruelty-free symbolic dove release.
sentences.zh: 没错，还有一场无动物虐待的象征性和平鸽放飞活动。

sentences.en: A mysterious figure rode on a metal horse down the Seine, unfurling massive dove wings.
sentences.zh: 一个神秘人物骑着一匹金属马沿塞纳河而下，展开了巨大的鸽子翅膀。

sentences.en: It was weird and wonderful.
sentences.zh: 既诡异又精彩。

sentences.en: This week, we're presenting a freshly remixed pair of older Olympic stories from 99PI.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将呈现两段来自99PI的、重新混音制作的早期奥运会故事。

sentences.en: We'll hear more about some long-lost Olympic events that we think should definitely be brought back.
sentences.zh: 我们将听到更多关于一些早已消失、我们认为绝对应该恢复的奥运项目的故事。

sentences.en: But first, this 2017 episode about the iconic design of the 1968 Games in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 但首先，是这集关于1968年墨西哥城奥运会标志性设计的2017年节目。

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 尽情享受吧。

sentences.en: The United States leads the Olympics in medal awards and is just about supreme in the sprint races.
sentences.zh: 美国在奥运会奖牌榜上领先，在短跑项目上也几乎占据绝对优势。

sentences.en: On October 16th, 1968, American sprinters Tommy Smith and John Carlos climbed onto the podium at the Mexico City Olympics to accept their medals.
sentences.zh: 1968年10月16日，美国短跑运动员汤米·史密斯和约翰·卡洛斯登上墨西哥城奥运会的领奖台领取奖牌。

sentences.en: Yesterday, they came in first and third in the 200-meter dash.
sentences.zh: 就在昨天，他们在200米短跑中分别获得了第一名和第三名。

sentences.en: Smith had won gold.
sentences.zh: 史密斯赢得了金牌。

sentences.en: Carlos had won bronze.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯赢得了铜牌。

sentences.en: As the national anthem began to play, the men, both African-American, bowed their heads and raised their fists in the Black Power salute.
sentences.zh: 当国歌奏响时，这两位非裔美国运动员低下了头，举起拳头行“黑人权力”的敬礼。

sentences.en: That's producer Claire Mullen.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人克莱尔·穆伦。

sentences.en: They kept their fists raised until the last notes of the anthem faded away.
sentences.zh: 他们一直高举着拳头，直到国歌的最后一个音符消散。

sentences.en: The gesture was a statement of Black pride and defiance.
sentences.zh: 这一手势表达了黑人的骄傲与反抗。

sentences.en: It's still considered one of the most overtly political statements made in the history of the modern Olympic Games.
sentences.zh: 它至今仍被认为是现代奥运会历史上最具政治色彩的表态之一。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the only politically significant moment at the Olympics that year.
sentences.zh: 但那并不是那一年奥运会上唯一具有政治意义的时刻。

sentences.en: A Mexican hurdler named Enriqueta Basilio became the first woman to ever light the Olympic cauldron.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫恩里克塔·巴西利奥的墨西哥跨栏运动员成为点燃奥运圣火的第一位女性。

sentences.en: A Czech gymnast beat out Soviet gymnasts for the overall women's title just two months after the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 就在苏联入侵捷克斯洛伐克两个月后，一名捷克体操运动员在女子个人全能项目上击败了苏联体操运动员。

sentences.en: It was also the first time a Latin American city or even a Spanish-speaking country had hosted the Games.
sentences.zh: 这也是奥运会历史上第一次由拉丁美洲城市甚至是西班牙语国家主办。

sentences.en: It was a big deal to have hundreds of thousands of international travelers come visit Mexico.
sentences.zh: 数十万国际游客来到墨西哥参观，这是一件大事。

sentences.en: The Mexican government saw the Olympics as an announcement to the world.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥政府将奥运会视为向世界发布的一则宣告。

sentences.en: Mexico City had arrived as a major international metropolis.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城已跻身国际大都市之列。

sentences.en: So almost everything about the 1968 Olympics felt revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 因此，1968年奥运会的几乎所有方面都给人一种革命性的感觉。

sentences.en: Including the design of it.
sentences.zh: 包括它的设计。

sentences.en: The images and logos associated with the 1968 Olympics were ubiquitous at the time.
sentences.zh: 与1968年奥运会相关的图像和标志在当时无处不在。

sentences.en: They were plastered all over the city.
sentences.zh: 它们贴满了整座城市。

sentences.en: This complete design campaign would become one of the most famous in Olympic history.
sentences.zh: 这一完整的设计活动将成为奥运史上最著名的设计之一。

sentences.en: And it would set a whole new standard for Games to come.
sentences.zh: 它为未来的奥运会树立了全新的标准。

sentences.en: But these government-commissioned designs would also be co-opted by local activists.
sentences.zh: 但这些由政府委托的设计后来也被当地的活动人士所借用。

sentences.en: Who wanted to reveal the darker political reality in Mexico that was hidden behind the beautiful, glossy imagery of the 1968 Games.
sentences.zh: 他们想要揭露隐藏在1968年奥运会美丽、光鲜的形象背后的、更黑暗的政治现实。

sentences.en: In the decades leading up to the 1968 Olympics, Mexico had gone through a period of major economic growth.
sentences.zh: 在通往1968年奥运会的几十年里，墨西哥经历了一段经济高速增长的时期。

sentences.en: It became known as the Mexican Miracle.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“墨西哥奇迹”。

sentences.en: The Mexican Miracle, typically, you know, historians conventionally speak about it as a period spanning from the mid-1940s to the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: “墨西哥奇迹”，通常情况下，你知道的，历史学家传统上认为这是一个从20世纪40年代中期持续到60年代末的时期。

sentences.en: The country had rapidly industrialized, rapidly urbanized, and its capital, Mexico City, had grown into this enormous, sprawling metropolis.
sentences.zh: 这个国家迅速实现了工业化和城市化，其首都墨西哥城已经成长为一个巨大、蔓延的大都市。

sentences.en: The city grew faster than it ever had in Mexico's modern history.
sentences.zh: 这座城市的增长速度超过了墨西哥现代历史上的任何时期。

sentences.en: That's Luis Castaneda.
sentences.zh: 那是路易斯·卡斯塔涅达。

sentences.en: He's the author of Spectacular Mexico, Design, Propaganda, and the 1968 Olympics.
sentences.zh: 他是《壮观的墨西哥：设计、宣传与1968年奥运会》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Because of its size and layout, Mexico City was a challenging place to host a major international event like the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 由于其规模和布局，墨西哥城是一个举办奥运会这样的大型国际活动颇具挑战性的地方。

sentences.en: Mexico City was sprawling and spreading, still at the height of its miracle.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城仍在不断扩张和蔓延，当时正处于其“奇迹”的巅峰时期。

sentences.en: I mean, even until the Olympics are literally about to happen, there are all these doubts about whether the Mexican government will be organized enough to undertake the whole,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，甚至直到奥运会即将开幕之际，人们仍然对墨西哥政府是否有足够的组织能力来承办这一切充满种种怀疑，

sentences.en: a spectacle of that magnitude.
sentences.zh: 这是一场规模空前的视觉盛宴。

sentences.en: The Olympic organizers needed to show that their metropolis was safe, navigable, cohesive, and, you know, exciting.
sentences.zh: 奥运会组织者需要证明他们的大都市是安全、畅通、凝聚力强且令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: They wanted to create a visual identity for the Olympics, to really sell Mexico City to all these visitors seeing it for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们想为奥运会创造一个视觉识别系统，向所有第一次来到这里的游客推销墨西哥城。

sentences.en: So, they decided to hold an international competition to find a designer who would create a logo and graphic design campaign for the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们决定举办一场国际比赛，寻找一位为奥运会创作标志和平面设计活动的伟大设计师。

sentences.en: They wanted something that looked cosmopolitan and contemporary, and distinctly Mexican.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一种既具有大都市风范和现代感、又具有鲜明墨西哥特色的人。

sentences.en: And this is where an unlikely character comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个意想不到的人物登场的地方。

sentences.en: I'm Lance Wyman.
sentences.zh: 我是兰斯·怀曼。

sentences.en: I'm a designer.
sentences.zh: 我是一名设计师。

sentences.en: I work here in New York.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约工作。

sentences.en: In 1966, Lance Wyman was a 29-year-old graphic designer.
sentences.zh: 1966年，兰斯·怀曼是一名29岁的平面设计师。

sentences.en: When he heard about the competition, he knew that he and his design partner, Peter Murdoch, had to get on the short list of contenders.
sentences.zh: 当他听到这个比赛的消息时，他知道自己和设计搭档彼得·默多克必须入围候选名单。

sentences.en: This list included design teams from all over the world who would come down to Mexico City for a two-week trial run.
sentences.zh: 这份名单包括来自世界各地的设计团队，他们将来到墨西哥城进行为期两周的试用。

sentences.en: After their two weeks, each team would present their design for consideration.
sentences.zh: 两周后，每个团队都要展示他们的设计供评审。

sentences.en: And we got on the list to go down in November of 1966, and Peter and I had just started out.
sentences.zh: 我们在1966年11月入选并前往那里，当时我和彼得刚开始创业。

sentences.en: We didn't have any money, so we could only afford one-way tickets.
sentences.zh: 我们没有钱，所以只能买得起单程机票。

sentences.en: They hopped on the plane with their one-way tickets and landed in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着单程机票跳上飞机，降落在墨西哥城。

sentences.en: By the way, neither of them had ever visited Mexico before.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们两人以前从未去过墨西哥。

sentences.en: They didn't really know anything about the country.
sentences.zh: 他们对这个国家真的一无所知。

sentences.en: If they were going to design a logo to represent Mexico, Wyman and Murdoch would have to learn a lot.
sentences.zh: 如果要设计一个代表墨西哥的标志，怀曼和默多克必须学习很多东西。

sentences.en: And faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且要快。

sentences.en: They started where most tourists start, by visiting museuMs.
sentences.zh: 他们从大多数游客开始的地方入手，参观博物馆。

sentences.en: They spent a lot of time at the Museum of Anthropology, where they studied artifacts from pre-Columbian Mexico, like the Aztec sunstone and ancient Mayan murals.
sentences.zh: 他们在人类学博物馆花了大量时间，研究前哥伦布时期墨西哥的文物，比如阿兹特克太阳石和古代玛雅壁画。

sentences.en: I actually was floored by some of the early cultures because they were doing things in a contemporary way with geometry and with graphics.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我对早期的一些文化感到震撼，因为他们用几何图形和平面设计以一种非常现代的方式在做事。

sentences.en: The bold lines and bright colors and geometric shapes reminded Wyman of the kind of op art that was popular among contemporary artists back in New York.
sentences.zh: 大胆的线条、明亮的色彩和几何形状让怀曼想起了当时在纽约当代艺术家中流行的欧普艺术。

sentences.en: Op art, or optical art, uses contrast, geometry, and other tricks to give the viewer the impression of movement.
sentences.zh: 欧普艺术，即光学艺术，利用对比、几何和其他技巧给观者以运动的错觉。

sentences.en: And so, informed by both indigenous artifacts and modern op art, Wyman came up with a logo that riffed on the five rings of the Olympic symbol.
sentences.zh: 因此，在本土文物和现代欧普艺术的启发下，怀曼设计了一个借用奥运会五环标志的标识。

sentences.en: I realized that the geometry of the five rings could be integrated with the year of the event, 68.
sentences.zh: 我意识到五环的几何形状可以与赛事的年份“68”结合起来。

sentences.en: He superimposed the digits 6 and 8 over the classic Olympic rings.
sentences.zh: 他将数字6和8重叠在经典的奥运五环之上。

sentences.en: The circles on the rings radiated out from the circles in the digits, and it created a hypnotic stripe effect.
sentences.zh: 环上的圆圈从数字中的圆圈辐射开来，创造出一种催眠般的条纹效果。

sentences.en: And from that, I developed the typography to make the word Mexico.
sentences.zh: 在此基础上，我开发了用来拼写“Mexico”一词的字体。

sentences.en: It's this very groovy-looking typography made of three parallel stripes.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常时髦的字体，由三条平行线组成。

sentences.en: Wyman created a logo that he considered both very modern and quintessentially Mexican.
sentences.zh: 怀曼创造了一个他认为既非常现代又极具墨西哥风情的标志。

sentences.en: The end of the two weeks came, and we started making prints of the Mexico 68 logotype, and people from publications and people from the public relations, they wanted copies of it.
sentences.zh: 两周的时间到了，我们开始打印“Mexico 68”字标，出版界和公关界的人都想要它的复本。

sentences.en: And we were working like crazy, making copies and doing all of that.
sentences.zh: 我们像疯了一样工作，复印文件，做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And then Wyman realized that no one actually told him yet if he had the job, so he asked one of the organizers.
sentences.zh: 然后怀曼意识到还没有人告诉他是否得到了这份工作，于是他问了一位组织者。

sentences.en: I said, did we win?
sentences.zh: 我说，我们赢了吗？

sentences.en: He goes, oh, I guess so.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我想是的。

sentences.en: Wyman had created a stunning logo and typeface for the competition.
sentences.zh: 怀曼为这次比赛创作了一个令人惊叹的标志和字体。

sentences.en: But choosing this white guy who had never been to Mexico before was a bit problematic.
sentences.zh: 但是选择一个从未去过墨西哥的白人确实有点问题。

sentences.en: It's not that unusual for people not born in Mexico for artists and people in culture and the arts to be involved with these kinds of state-sponsored campaigns.
sentences.zh: 对于非墨西哥出生的人来说，让艺术家和文化艺术界人士参与这种国家资助的宣传活动并不是什么稀罕事。

sentences.en: It's not entirely unprecedented, but it's still a very unique situation, especially given the fact that, you know, this is a very, very significant project.
sentences.zh: 这并非完全史无前例，但仍然是一个非常独特的情况，特别是考虑到这是一个非常非常重大的项目。

sentences.en: That's author Luis Castañeda again.
sentences.zh: 再次听到作者路易斯·卡斯塔涅达的讲述。

sentences.en: What is very striking, almost shocking, perhaps, is that the fact that, of course, Lance Wyman is very much unproven as a designer.
sentences.zh: 非常引人注目、甚至近乎令人震惊的是，兰斯·怀曼作为一名设计师其实完全没有名气。

sentences.en: He's very young.
sentences.zh: 他非常年轻。

sentences.en: He hasn't had much time to do much yet.
sentences.zh: 他还没有多少时间做过太多事情。

sentences.en: And yet somehow he is given this very high degree of responsibility as part of the design campaign.
sentences.zh: 然而，不知何故，作为设计活动的一部分，他被赋予了如此高的责任。

sentences.en: Wyman and Murdoch ended up staying in Mexico for two years to work on the campaign.
sentences.zh: 怀曼和默多克最终在墨西哥呆了两年，为活动工作。

sentences.en: And, along with a team of designers, many of them Mexican, they came up with ways to use their typeface, logo, and other designs all over the city.
sentences.zh: 并且，与一个设计团队（其中许多人是墨西哥人）一起，他们想出了在全城使用他们的字体、标志和其他设计的各种方法。

sentences.en: The hypnotic stripes were turned into striped uniforms for the event's workers and volunteers.
sentences.zh: 催眠般的条纹被制作成了赛事工作人员和志愿者的条纹制服。

sentences.en: The patterns and colors used in the logo ended up on hats, posted stamps, balloons, all sorts of products to hype the impending games.
sentences.zh: 标志中使用的图案和颜色最终出现在帽子、邮票、气球以及各种为宣传即将到来的奥运会而制作的产品上。

sentences.en: And these objects range from very small objects, all kinds of memorabilia, you know, things from ashtrays and furniture or apparel, all the way to the stadiuMs.
sentences.zh: 这些物品从小物件、各种纪念品，比如烟灰缸、家具或服装，一直到体育场馆应有尽有。

sentences.en: Stadiums across the city were painted with these radiating op art patterns.
sentences.zh: 全城的体育场馆都涂上了这些放射状的欧普艺术图案。

sentences.en: Bright colors decorated sidewalks and walls and plazas.
sentences.zh: 明亮的色彩装点着人行道、墙壁和广场。

sentences.en: And these bright, hypnotic designs didn't just give the Olympic Games a visual coherence.
sentences.zh: 这些明亮、催眠般的设计不仅赋予了奥运会视觉上的一致性。

sentences.en: The graphic design language of the Olympics expanded into an entire system that helped visitors navigate the massive metropolis.
sentences.zh: 奥运会的平面设计语言扩展成了一个完整的系统，帮助游客在这座庞大的大都市中辨别方向。

sentences.en: To do this, Wyman made simple, color-coded icons to represent every sporting event.
sentences.zh: 为此，怀曼制作了简单、有颜色编码的图标来代表每个体育项目。

sentences.en: They were not stick figures, but they were focused more on, you know, a part of the body or a piece of the equipment or a combination of the two.
sentences.zh: 它们不是火柴人，而是更多地关注身体的一部分、一件装备或两者的结合。

sentences.en: Gymnastics, for example, was represented by a hand gripping a single suspended ring.
sentences.zh: 例如，体操是用一只抓着单吊环的手来代表的。

sentences.en: Track and field had its icon.
sentences.zh: 田径有它的图标。

sentences.en: Boxing had its icon.
sentences.zh: 拳击有它的图标。

sentences.en: So on the ticket, you knew what your ticket was for by the icon only.
sentences.zh: 所以在票上，仅凭图标你就能知道你的票是看什么项目的。

sentences.en: So if you're visiting from Japan and didn't speak any Spanish, you'd see, say, the soccer icon on a green background.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是从日本来访且不会说西班牙语，你会看到一个绿色背景上的足球图标。

sentences.en: And you'd follow the green signs to the stadium where the soccer would be.
sentences.zh: 然后你会沿着绿色标志走到踢足球的体育场。

sentences.en: And this system wasn't just for sports.
sentences.zh: 这个系统不仅适用于体育运动。

sentences.en: Wyman and the team made universally understandable icons for 19 cultural events happening around the city as well.
sentences.zh: 怀曼和团队还为全城举办的19个文化活动制作了普遍易懂的图标。

sentences.en: We had children's painting.
sentences.zh: 我们有儿童绘画。

sentences.en: We had folk dancing.
sentences.zh: 我们有民间舞蹈。

sentences.en: We had science programming.
sentences.zh: 我们有科学节目。

sentences.en: By following these cultural icons, visitors could continue to entertain themselves and explore the city after the sporting events were over.
sentences.zh: 通过跟随这些文化图标，游客在体育赛事结束后可以继续自娱自乐并探索这座城市。

sentences.en: The 1968 Olympics had been decreed Los Juegos de la Paz, the Games of Peace.
sentences.zh: 1968年奥运会被宣布为“和平运动会”（Los Juegos de la Paz）。

sentences.en: So Wyman designed a little outline of a dove which shop owners all over the city were given to stick in their windows.
sentences.zh: 因此，怀曼设计了一个小鸽子的轮廓，全城的店主都被发给了一个，以便贴在他们的窗户上。

sentences.en: Between the logo, the typeface, the colors, the icons, and the doves, Wyman created a visual identity that saturated the whole city.
sentences.zh: 通过标志、字体、颜色、图标和鸽子，怀曼创造了一个渗透到整个城市的视觉识别系统。

sentences.en: It was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它无处不在。

sentences.en: It was a total design campaign.
sentences.zh: 这是一场全面的设计活动。

sentences.en: Total design campaign, right?
sentences.zh: 全面的设计活动，对吧？

sentences.en: There's the idea of total design, that every single thing, idea, place, object associated with the Olympics is immediately and powerfully recognizable as part of a whole.
sentences.zh: 存在一种“整体设计”的理念，即与奥运会相关的每一件单一的事情、想法、地点、物体，都能让人立刻强烈地认出它是整体的一部分。

sentences.en: And the completeness of the campaign would set a precedent for years to come.
sentences.zh: 这场活动的完整性为未来的岁月树立了先例。

sentences.en: I think it's safe to say that although design and architecture and the arts in general had been very powerfully associated with Olympics before Mexico 68,
sentences.zh: 我认为可以肯定地说，尽管在1968年墨西哥奥运会之前，设计、建筑和一般艺术就已经与奥运会有着非常强烈的联系，

sentences.en: it's really after Mexico 68 that it becomes a kind of standard expectation of design campaigns associated with these kinds of events.
sentences.zh: 但真正从1968年墨西哥奥运会之后，它才成为与这类活动相关的设计活动的某种标准期望。

sentences.en: While Lance Wyman was designing this extensive campaign, he was holed up, swamped with work, and he really didn't get a chance to go out much.
sentences.zh: 当兰斯·怀曼在设计这个庞大的活动时，他被关在屋里，工作堆积如山，根本没有什么机会出去走走。

sentences.en: Nose to the grindstone, really, almost through the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 真的是脚踏实地、埋头苦干，几乎贯穿了整个过程。

sentences.en: We were pretty isolated at the Olympic Committee.
sentences.zh: 我们在奥组委相当孤立。

sentences.en: He didn't see the protest movement growing in the city around him.
sentences.zh: 他没有看到周围城市中不断壮大的抗议运动。

sentences.en: The movement was led by students who believed the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party catered to wealthy Mexicans rather than the poor, rural, and working class.
sentences.zh: 这场运动由学生领导，他们认为长期执政的革命制度党迎合了富裕的墨西哥人，而不是贫困、农村和工人阶级。

sentences.en: The country had been experiencing huge economic growth, but millions of people had been left behind.
sentences.zh: 这个国家一直在经历巨大的经济增长，但数百万人民却被抛在了后面。

sentences.en: The Mexican miracle hadn't reached everyone.
sentences.zh: “墨西哥奇迹”并没有惠及每一个人。

sentences.en: The government was talking of the Mexican miracle, even though in the reality of those days, things were not as happy as they appeared.
sentences.zh: 政府在谈论“墨西哥奇迹”，尽管在那几天的现实中，事情并不像表面看起来那么高兴。

sentences.en: These are excerpts from interviews with students involved in the protests against Mexico's single-party government, courtesy of our friends at Radio Diaries.
sentences.zh: 这些是采访参与反对墨西哥一党制政府抗议的学生的摘录，由我们的朋友“广播日记”（Radio Diaries）提供。

sentences.en: In the 60s, we were still a country where the government controlled everything.
sentences.zh: 在60年代，我们仍然是一个由政府控制一切的国家。

sentences.en: Presidents were the equivalent of monarchs.
sentences.zh: 总统就相当于君主。

sentences.en: I mean, it was forbidden to demonstrate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，示威游行是禁止的。

sentences.en: You could not go and express your dissent.
sentences.zh: 你不能去表达你的异见。

sentences.en: And for the students, protesting the government meant protesting against the Olympics themselves, the so-called Games of Peace.
sentences.zh: 对于学生来说，抗议政府意味着抗议奥运会本身，即所谓的“和平运动会”。

sentences.en: Olympics are, I think maybe by design, by definition, always about propaganda on some level or another.
sentences.zh: 奥运会，我想也许按设计、按定义，在某种程度上总是关乎宣传。

sentences.en: And so what the Olympics sought to present as a kind of happy picture of social harmony and as a kind of very sanitized idea of how modernization happens was, of course,
sentences.zh: 因此，奥运会试图呈现的那种社会和谐的快乐画面以及关于现代化如何发生的极其美化的概念，当然，

sentences.en: not the reality of what many of these inhabitants of the city experienced.
sentences.zh: 并不是许多这些城市居民所经历的现实。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of protesters took to the streets repeatedly throughout 1968.
sentences.zh: 在1968年的整个过程中，成千上万的抗议者屡次走上街头。

sentences.en: We were urban middle class, low middle class, bunch of young people.
sentences.zh: 我们是城市中产阶级、下中产阶级，一群年轻人。

sentences.en: It was, in a symbolic way, the clash of a new Mexico and an old Mexico.
sentences.zh: 从象征意义上讲，这是新墨西哥与旧墨西哥的冲突。

sentences.en: You have a middle class with eyes closed and a group of students saying, this was not a democracy and this is not working.
sentences.zh: 你有一个闭着眼睛的中产阶级和一群说这不是民主、这行不通的学生。

sentences.en: Again and again, police had come out and violently dispersed protesters with clouds of tear gas.
sentences.zh: 警察一次又一次地出动，用催泪瓦斯驱散抗议者。

sentences.en: As the Olympics neared and as international attention turned towards Mexico City, the government was desperate to make the unrest go away.
sentences.zh: 随着奥运会日益临近，国际社会的目光投向了墨西哥城，政府急于让这场骚乱平息下来。

sentences.en: On October 2nd, just 10 days before the Games of Peace were set to begin,
sentences.zh: 10月2日，就在和平奥运会开幕式前仅仅10天，

sentences.en: thousands of students gathered at Tlatelolco Square in the northeast of Mexico City to demand the release of people who had been locked up at a previous proteSt.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的学生聚集在墨西哥城东北部的特拉特洛尔科广场，要求释放此前在抗议活动中被关押的人员。

sentences.en: It was a quiet gathering of people with signs walking slowly around the plaza.
sentences.zh: 这是一场宁静的集会，人们举着标语，在广场上缓缓踱步。

sentences.en: And we looked back and there was all these infantry troops.
sentences.zh: 我们往回一看，全都是步兵。

sentences.en: They started to advance towards the crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们开始向人群推进。

sentences.en: And at some point, we heard some shots.
sentences.zh: 不知在什么时候，我们听到了枪声。

sentences.en: We didn't know where they came from.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道枪声是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: And seconds later, how do you say in English, all hell broke loose.
sentences.zh: 几秒钟后，英语里怎么说来着，乱成了一团。

sentences.en: Soldiers opened fire on the protesters.
sentences.zh: 士兵向抗议者开枪。

sentences.en: To this day, we don't know exactly how many students died in the massacre.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我们仍然不知道在大屠杀中有多少学生丧生。

sentences.en: But the number is likely in the hundreds.
sentences.zh: 但死伤人数很可能数以百计。

sentences.en: This is a peaceful demonstration.
sentences.zh: 这是一场和平游行。

sentences.en: The army was circling this plaza called the Plaza to Three Cultures.
sentences.zh: 军队包围了这个被称为三文化广场的广场。

sentences.en: The scene was cleared before there could be an accurate body count.
sentences.zh: 在能够准确统计尸体数量之前，现场就被清理干净了。

sentences.en: The blood was washed away.
sentences.zh: 血迹被冲洗得一干二净。

sentences.en: Thousands of protesters were arrested and locked up.
sentences.zh: 数千名抗议者被捕并关押。

sentences.en: The government took great pains to cover their tracks.
sentences.zh: 政府煞费苦心地掩盖他们的行踪。

sentences.en: The amount of students who were shot and many others were imprisoned for quite some time was, you know, covered up.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，中枪的学生数量以及许多被关押相当长时间的人，都被掩盖了。

sentences.en: The government claimed that the students had fired first to provoke the military.
sentences.zh: 政府声称是学生率先开枪挑衅军方。

sentences.en: Evidence has since come to light that disproves that claim.
sentences.zh: 此后曝光的证据推翻了这种说法。

sentences.en: It's an extremely shocking event for a long time, kind of suppressed in Mexican national memory.
sentences.zh: 这是一场极其震惊的事件，长期以来在墨西哥的民族记忆中被某种程度地压制。

sentences.en: And in many ways, it is the crux of the crisis that sets the stage for the, in a very, very dramatic sense, for the Olympics themselves.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，它正是这场危机的核心，以一种极其戏剧化的方式，为奥运会本身奠定了基调。

sentences.en: The massacre was so horribly devastating that, of course, Lance Wyman heard about it.
sentences.zh: 这场大屠杀是如此惨烈，兰斯·怀曼当然也听说了。

sentences.en: When I heard about it and how severe it was, it was a difficult situation because I felt I was working for the government and I couldn't do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 当我听到这个消息以及它的严重性时，处境非常艰难，因为我觉得自己是在为政府工作，却对此无能为力。

sentences.en: But he says he really empathized with the students.
sentences.zh: 但他说他非常感同身受那些学生。

sentences.en: I wasn't much older than they were, so I had that feeling.
sentences.zh: 我比他们大不了多少，所以我有那种感触。

sentences.en: Like, I might have felt good if I just walked away from the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 就像，如果我直接一走了之，我心里可能会好受一点。

sentences.en: Wyman felt stuck in the middle.
sentences.zh: 怀曼觉得自己陷入了两难境地。

sentences.en: But in a way, he didn't need to choose between the government and the protesters.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，他不需要在政府和抗议者之间做出选择。

sentences.en: His designs found a way to serve both sides.
sentences.zh: 他的设计找到了为双方服务的方法。

sentences.en: Students began imitating Wyman's images and co-opting them.
sentences.zh: 学生们开始模仿怀曼的图形，并将其挪为己用。

sentences.en: They took a poster he made with a silhouetted image of runners racing and turned it into silhouettes of troops beating people with batons.
sentences.zh: 他们把他制作的一张印有奔跑者剪影的海报，改成了军人用警棍殴打行人的剪影。

sentences.en: They used his signature typography to create anti-government posters.
sentences.zh: 他们用他标志性的字体来创作反政府海报。

sentences.en: And that very simple image of a dove in all the shop windows?
sentences.zh: 还有所有商店橱窗里那张极其简单的和平鸽图像？

sentences.en: Students went around the city spraying a small burst of bright red paint over the dove's chest, like it had been shot.
sentences.zh: 学生们走遍全城，在和平鸽的胸口喷上一小撮鲜红的油漆，就像它中枪了一样。

sentences.en: They were playing with the propaganda of the Olympics and hinting at a darker political reality.
sentences.zh: 他们在玩弄奥运会的宣传，并暗示着更黑暗的政治现实。

sentences.en: And Wyman, he liked it.
sentences.zh: 而怀曼，他很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: He made a design campaign so ubiquitous, so resonant, that the resistance could use it too.
sentences.zh: 他创作了一套无处不在、极具共鸣的设计方案，以至于抵抗力量也能使用它。

sentences.en: And I've always been questioned, well, why do you feel good about that?
sentences.zh: 一直有人质问我，好吧，你为什么对此感觉良好呢？

sentences.en: And I guess that's why, because I was in a situation where I was kind of torn.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是原因吧，因为我当时处于一种左右为难的境地。

sentences.en: I was very sympathetic as far as what was happening to the students, but I was also very not wanting to see the Olympics be stopped.
sentences.zh: 我非常同情学生们的遭遇，但我也极其不希望看到奥运会被叫停。

sentences.en: And they weren't stopped.
sentences.zh: 而奥运会并没有被叫停。

sentences.en: On October 12th, 1968, the Games began on schedule, as if nothing out of the ordinary had happened.
sentences.zh: 1968年10月12日，奥运会如期开幕，仿佛什么不寻常的事情都没有发生过一样。

sentences.en: The 1968 Olympics went on to become one of the most important in the history of the Games, marked not only by athletic achievement, but by open political defiance.
sentences.zh: 1968年奥运会成为奥运史上最重要的几届之一，其标志不仅在于体育成就，更在于公开的政治抗争。

sentences.en: Do you think you represented all black athletes in doing this?
sentences.zh: 你认为自己这样做代表了所有的黑人运动员吗？

sentences.en: I can say I represented black America.
sentences.zh: 我可以代表黑人美国。

sentences.en: I'm very proud to be a black man and also to have won a gold medal.
sentences.zh: 我为自己是一个黑人，并且赢得了一枚金牌而感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: Mexico 68 also set a new precedent for how governments would use design to promote their country's image to the international community, for better or for worse.
sentences.zh: 无论好坏，墨西哥68也为各国政府如何利用设计向国际社会推广国家形象树立了新的先例。

sentences.en: The 68 Games also left a permanent mark on Mexico City's infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 1968年奥运会也给墨西哥城的城市基础设施留下了永久的印记。

sentences.en: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in the world.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城是世界上最大的城市之一。

sentences.en: It's the largest metropolitan area in North America.
sentences.zh: 它是北美最大的都市圈。

sentences.en: Around 4.4 million people ride on Mexico City's metro system every day, including producer Claire Mullen, who visited a couple months ago.
sentences.zh: 每天大约有440万人乘坐墨西哥城的地铁系统，其中包括几个月前曾去参观过的制片人克莱尔·马伦。

sentences.en: I'm in the metro on the pink line at Cuauhtémoc, which has an eagle icon.
sentences.zh: 我正坐在地铁粉色线上夸特莫克站，这里的标志是一只老鹰。

sentences.en: Mexico City's metro is incredibly crowded and very extensive, and yet it is often recognized as one of the easiest rail systems to navigate, partly because of its iconography.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥城的地铁拥挤异常且四通八达，但它却常被认为是导向最清晰、最容易搭乘的轨道系统之一，这部分要归功于它的视觉符号。

sentences.en: La Católica, which is a big ship.
sentences.zh: 天主教圣母站，是一艘大船。

sentences.en: It looks like a pirate ship without the pirate symbol.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像一艘没有海盗标志的海盗船。

sentences.en: And then we have Merced, where there are six apples in a crate.
sentences.zh: 然后是莫塞德站，那里有一个板条箱装着六个苹果。

sentences.en: And those icons are there, thanks in part to Lance Wyman.
sentences.zh: 这些标志之所以存在，部分要归功于兰斯·怀曼。

sentences.en: The metro was supposed to make its debut during the Olympics, but excavators kept unearthing ancient architecture in the path of the tracks, and the opening was delayed.
sentences.zh: 地铁本应在奥运会期间首次亮相，但挖掘机在轨道沿线不断发掘出古代建筑，导致开通时间延期。

sentences.en: But Wyman was still involved in its design, specifically its map.
sentences.zh: 但怀曼依然参与了它的设计，特别是它的地图。

sentences.en: He employed the same visual system he developed for the Olympics to help international visitors navigate the trains.
sentences.zh: 他采用了他为奥运会开发的同一套视觉系统，来帮助国际游客辨识火车路线。

sentences.en: In the Olympics, we relied on the graphics, and I thought, well, why can't a city do that?
sentences.zh: 在奥运会期间，我们依赖图形，我想，为什么一个城市不能那样做呢？

sentences.en: So Wyman color-coded each line and created a unique icon for every single stop.
sentences.zh: 因此，怀曼用颜色区分了每条线路，并为每一个站点创作了一个独特的图标。

sentences.en: So, even if you're visiting from Japan and can't read any Spanish at all, you can say to yourself,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你是从日本来的游客，完全看不懂西班牙语，你也可以对自己说，

sentences.en: I want to take the pink line to the stop with the grasshopper on it.
sentences.zh: 我想坐粉色线去那个有蚂蚱图案的车站。

sentences.en: The station that stopped at Chapultepec Park, Chapultepec means grasshopper hill in the Nahuatl, the Aztec language, so I used the grasshopper.
sentences.zh: 那个在查普尔特佩克公园停靠的车站，在阿兹特克语纳瓦特尔语中，查普尔特佩克的意思是蚂蚱山，所以我用了蚂蚱。

sentences.en: Again, some Mexicans took issue with this young foreigner coming in to design something that would be such a huge part of their city.
sentences.zh: 同样，一些墨西哥人对这个年轻的外国人跑来设计他们城市中如此重要的一部分感到不满。

sentences.en: But eventually, Mexican designers took up the project and made it their own.
sentences.zh: 但最终，墨西哥设计师接手了这个项目，并将其打造为他们自己的作品。

sentences.en: You know, I designed the first three lines of the Metro, and all the, they have 12 lines now, and they were designed by Mexican designers,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我设计了地铁的前三条线，所有这些，他们现在有12条线了，都是由墨西哥设计师设计的，

sentences.en: and some of these are better than I did on the original line.
sentences.zh: 其中一些比我原先设计的线路还要出色。

sentences.en: After the Olympics, after the Metro, Wyman did some more work for Mexico, like the design for the 1970 World Cup.
sentences.zh: 奥运会之后，地铁之后，怀曼为墨西哥做了一些额外的工作，比如1970年世界杯的设计。

sentences.en: But he went back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但他回到了美国。

sentences.en: Wyman went on to design more maps.
sentences.zh: 怀曼继续设计更多的地图。

sentences.en: Big ones, like for the National Zoo and the D.C.
sentences.zh: 大型的地图，比如为国家动物园和华盛顿特区

sentences.en: metro system.
sentences.zh: 地铁系统设计的地图。

sentences.en: Although, none of them used symbols and icons and colors as completely as in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，其中没有一个像墨西哥城那样全面地运用了符号、图标和颜色。

sentences.en: The clear iconography of the metro system is a reminder of a complicated and sometimes terrible period in Mexico City's history.
sentences.zh: 地铁系统清晰的视觉符号，让人想起墨西哥城历史上复杂且有时糟糕的一段时期。

sentences.en: It's a simple design that invites you to explore the massive and complex metropolis.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单的设计，邀请你去探索这个巨大而复杂的都市。

sentences.en: It's a design that assures you that if you get lost, no matter where you're from or what language you speak,
sentences.zh: 这个设计向你保证，如果你迷路了，无论你来自哪里，说什么语言，

sentences.en: you can find your way around and see the city for yourself.
sentences.zh: 你都能找到方向，亲眼领略这座城市。

sentences.en: After the break, an Olympic road not taken.
sentences.zh: 稍事休息后，我们将探讨一条未曾选择的奥运之路。

sentences.en: The Olympic Games seem almost timeless, going back to ancient Greece.
sentences.zh: 奥运会似乎是一个永恒的概念，可以追溯到古希腊。

sentences.en: So it can be easy to forget that the modern games as we know them today were only launched just over a century ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们很容易忘记，我们今天所知道的现代奥运会其实是一个多世纪前才刚刚创立的。

sentences.en: Last week, we heard about firefighting and tug-of-war, which tug-of-war has to come back in the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们听到了关于消防和拔河的介绍，拔河真该重返奥运会。

sentences.en: I mean, I think this might be my new mission in life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是我生活中的新使命。

sentences.en: But what about Olympic poetry?
sentences.zh: 但是奥运诗歌呢？

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad told us about it back in 2021.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔施塔德早在2021年就跟我们讲过。

sentences.en: To get things started, Roman, I'm going to have you read the first stanza of a poem.
sentences.zh: 为了开个好头，罗曼，我要请你朗读一首诗的第一节。

sentences.en: It's titled, Ode to Sport, and it was written in 1912, 16 years after the first modern Olympic Games.
sentences.zh: 它题为《体育颂》，创作于1912年，即第一届现代奥运会举办16年之后。

sentences.en: Okay, here it goes.
sentences.zh: 好的，开始啦。

sentences.en: O sport, pleasure of the gods, essence of life.

sentences.en: So he's at the forefront of Olympics in general, and that committee decided to host the very first modern International Olympics in 1896.

sentences.en: Well, not quite yet.

sentences.en: But then, after we'd had a couple of good, successful games, all centered around sports,
sentences.zh: 但是，在举办了几届以体育为中心、相当成功的赛事之后，

sentences.en: And so these creative competitions grew popular.

sentences.zh: 而其中一个副效应是，它们开始自然而然地吸引那些更像是有抱负的专业人士，甚至是资深的创意人员。
